fr:title.text: Claude skills for iterative Agda development

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Claude skills for iterative Agda development

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Design and ship one or more Claude Code skills that help an agent draft Agda code iteratively, using the Agda typechecker as the primary oracle instead of reading through the codebase until the context window is exhausted. Any pre-existing Agda skill is unused and should be treated as deprecated — replace rather than extend it.
Core iteration loop. The skill should enforce a hole-at-a-time workflow:

html:ul.html:li: Query the types and contexts of all open holes in the target file up front, so the agent has a work plan before editing.

For each hole, make one modular change, then typecheck. Do not advance to the next hole until the current edit typechecks cleanly and no unsolved metas (yellow) remain — yellow is failure, not success.
When stuck, prefer re-introducing {! !} over committing a guess. Let the compiler narrow the goal.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Runtime is a signal, not just a cost. Every typecheck and every agda --interaction command runs under a wall-clock budget:

html:ul.html:li: Hard cap around 20s per check or interaction — if Agda hasn't responded, treat the attempt as failed and abandon that route. Do not wait longer hoping it resolves.

Anything over ~5s is a warning sign for the vast majority of goals. Slow elaboration usually means the agent is fighting the typechecker: wrong lemma driving divergent unification, universe mismatch blowing up constraints, over-concrete instantiation, or reduction that should have been abstract / opaque. Treat the slowness as evidence the approach is wrong, not as something to wait out.

Prune aggressively on slow feedback. When a candidate term makes the typechecker crawl, back it out and try a structurally different approach (different lemma, different case-split order, more holes) rather than tweaking details of the slow term.
Some files legitimately take longer (large HITs, heavy transports). Allow a per-project override, but default to the tight budget.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Use the compiler as an oracle, not the codebase. Wrap agda --interaction (or --interaction-json) in a bash script so the agent can issue Cmd_goal_type_context_infer, Cmd_refine_or_intro, Cmd_make_case, Cmd_auto_maybe_all, and Cmd_compute programmatically. These narrowing tactics produce correct-by-construction skeletons and are far higher density than reading source.
Context-management rules (the failure mode to prevent: agent reads through stdlib / cubical until the window fills, compacts, then repeats without writing code):

html:ul.html:li: Prefer grep over Read for lemma discovery. Type signatures are one-liners; whole-file reads are almost never necessary.

Delegate library search to a subagent with a tight prompt ("find functions in Cubical.Foundations.* whose return type matches isEquiv _") so exploration fills the subagent's context, not the main one.
Exhaust the typechecker first. Before reading any file, the agent must have run goal/context inspection, auto, refine, and case-split on the current hole.
Budget exploration explicitly: at most N files read before the next compile attempt. When the budget is hit, write something so the typechecker's error narrows the search further.
Scratch-file discovered lemmas (Module.foo : T → U) so post-compaction the agent doesn't re-discover the same results.
Fail loudly. After K consecutive edits without a green typecheck, surface the blockage to the user rather than spiraling.
Single monolithic skill vs. several small ones (e.g. agda-fill-hole, agda-search-lemma, agda-check)?
Does the skill need project-aware setup (locate .agda-lib / Cubical / agda-stdlib roots) or can it assume the user's environment is already configured?
How should the skill handle Agsy timeouts and partial results from auto?
Cubical vs. vanilla Agda — same skill, or separate flavors for --cubical pragmas and HITs?

fr:title.text: Sketch: the CFG derivative parser internal to LambekD

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Sketch: the CFG derivative parser internal to LambekD

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Feasibility sketch for building the inductive derivative parser inside Lambek^{D} in Agda. The claim: it is definable and provable by combining the regex \delta + soundness on the brzozowski branch with \rhd /lob on the box branch; the one design decision is to put the guard in the datatype, and the one genuine risk is refl-time computation. Signatures below are schematic — proofs are holes, never postulates.

fr:title.text: Datatype: guard as a structural invariant

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Datatype: guard as a structural invariant

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The naive recursion δ c (var X) = δ c (def X) does not pass Agda's termination checker — def X is not a subterm and the keystone short-circuit is semantic. So encode the guard structurally, Greibach-style: a nonterminal is its finite list of guarded clauses ⌈c⌉ ⊗ tail.
fr:mainmatter.html:pre:
NT : Type -- finite context of nonterminals (e.g. Fin n)
data CFGDesc : Type where ⟨I⟩ ⟨⊥⟩ : CFGDesc -- ε , empty lit : ⟨ Alphabet ⟩ → CFGDesc -- ⌈c⌉ var : NT → CFGDesc -- nonterminal leaf _⊗_ _⊕_ : CFGDesc → CFGDesc → CFGDesc
record Production : Type where -- one nonterminal's productions field nullable : Bool -- is ε accepted? clauses : List (Alphabet × CFGDesc) -- guarded: (leading char , tail)
def : NT → Production -- the grammar = a table of productions
fr:mainmatter.html:p: The invariant "every var occurs behind a consumed terminal" is now unforgeable: a nonterminal reaches you only via a clauses entry, whose head is a literal. Unguarded grammars are not expressible.

fr:title.text: Nullability and derivative: both structural, Agda-accepted

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Nullability and derivative: both structural, Agda-accepted

fr:mainmatter.html:pre:
ν? : CFGDesc → Bool ν? ⟨I⟩ = true ν? ⟨⊥⟩ = false ν? (lit _) = false ν? (var X) = Production.nullable (def X) -- lookup, NOT recursive ν? (A ⊗ B) = ν? A and ν? B ν? (A ⊕ B) = ν? A or ν? B
δ : Alphabet → CFGDesc → CFGDesc δ c ⟨I⟩ = ⟨⊥⟩ δ c ⟨⊥⟩ = ⟨⊥⟩ δ c (lit c′) = if c == c′ then ⟨I⟩ else ⟨⊥⟩ δ c (A ⊕ B) = δ c A ⊕ δ c B δ c (A ⊗ B) = δ c A ⊗ B ⊕ (if ν? A then δ c B else ⟨⊥⟩) -- MUST short-circuit δ c (var X) = select c (Production.clauses (def X)) -- filter+strip, NO δ recursion where select c = foldr (λ (c′ , t) acc → if c == c′ then t ⊕ acc else acc) ⟨⊥⟩
fr:mainmatter.html:p: Both are structural recursions on CFGDesc: ν? (var X) and δ c (var X) are lookups, not recursive calls, so the termination checker is satisfied and the keystone is discharged by construction. CFGDesc is visibly closed under δ (residuals mention var, never a differentiated nonterminal).

Interpret into grammars — var as the guarded fixpoint (this is where the datatype's guard earns its keep, making the \mu well-defined via lob) — and prove the Brzozowski iso by induction on CFGDesc, its var case discharged by one \mu -unfold. Then the generic Löb parser.
fr:mainmatter.html:pre:
⟦_⟧ : CFGDesc → Grammar -- var ↦ μ (guarded), ⊗/⊕/lit/I/⊥ pointwise
δ-sound : (c : Alphabet)(G : CFGDesc) → ⟦ δ c G ⟧ ≅ ⟦ G ⟧ ⟜ lit c δ-sound c G = {!!} -- induction on G; var: μ-unfold + guard
Ans : CFGDesc → Grammar Ans G = ⟦ G ⟧ ⊕ ¬ ⟦ G ⟧
parse : (G : CFGDesc) → ⊤ ⊢ Ans G parse = lob λ rec G → {!!} -- ⊤ ≅ I ⊕ ⊕[c] ⌈c⌉ ⊗ ▷⊤ ; at I: ν? G ; at ⌈c⌉⊗▷: transport (rec (δ c G))
fr:mainmatter.html:p: The parse hole needs only: the guarded string decomposition of \top (box branch), the \rhd -guard discharge for the recursive call (⌈c⌉ ⊗ (−) factors through \rhd , sss-00EX), and δ-sound to move the answer across. Totality and correctness are then lob's uniqueness.

fr:title.text: The real risk: does it compute?

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The real risk: does it compute?

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Type-checking and proofs are the easy direction. Reducing parse dyck "aabb" by refl is the wall, and the constraints are known:

html:ul.html:li: lob reduces by refl only in Eq-world — the well-founded order must be Eq-valued or löbWF sticks under transp (reference: the Eq-vs-transp Löb issue).
Tensors must be SplittingEq from the start, or the hcomp/path-Splittings blowup that stalled witness evaluation returns.
Derivative descriptions grow; compaction (generic \bot /I unit rewrites) is optional for correctness but may be load-bearing for computation.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Empirically Dyck-style refl-evaluation was made tractable this way, while regex/greedy parsers did not terminate — so Dyck at refl is the first target; a general CFGDesc interpreter that computes is the open question, not a definability one.

html:ol.html:li: CFGDesc + Production datatype (guard structural), over the project's Alphabet.
ν?, δ (structural, total — no holes; termination free from the encoding).
⟦_⟧ and δ-sound (holes; induction on CFGDesc, reusing the brzozowski regex soundness pattern).
parse = lob … (hole; reuses box lob + \rhd decomposition).
Dyck instance; attempt refl-evaluation in Eq-world + SplittingEq; add compaction only if size blows up.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Steps 1–2 are self-contained and hole-free; 3–4 are the real proof work; 5 is the empirical gate. Reuses, does not rebuild, sss-00A6/sss-00A7 (regex \delta + soundness) and sss-00BE/sss-00BD (\rhd /lob).

Package the functor and its contractive strength as a ranked container / well-founded signature: shapes S x, positions Pos s, and an assignment of each position to a strictly-smaller index (the rank), so the functor is H₀ A x = Σ (s : S x) → Π (p : Pos s) → A (idx s p) with idx s p ≺ x. The strength is then generic.
The container was retired once in favour of an inline functor plus a two-line δ (which was lighter); the request is a clean optional interface, not a forced encoding.
This is the well-founded, single-sorted special case of the grammar indexed-inductive functor.

Every hylomorphism example currently hand-writes its functor and its contractive strength (the δ). Local contractivity should instead be a closed class with combinators, so larger contractive maps are assembled from smaller ones and δ is derived.
The closure conditions --- the guarded/metric semantics of the later modality:

html:ul.html:li: constant functors are contractive;
a recursive position guarded by \triangleright is contractive --- a bare variable is only non-expansive;
sums, products, and linear/tensor products preserve contractivity positionwise;
composition with a non-expansive functor preserves contractivity on either side.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: These are exactly the constructors of the grammar functor language, which is a syntactic form of this calculus. Pairs with the ranked-container interface.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Benchmark cause of slowness in Displayed.Instances.Sets.Properties

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Build standalone Agda programs that measure typechecking time as a function of reindexing depth and proof style, to confirm or falsify the hypothesis that the slowness in Displayed.Instances.Sets.Properties comes from nested reindexings combined with filler-at-a-time proofs (many transports over refl).

Constraint: do not edit the library. The benchmarks should be contrived client programs that import existing library code and exercise the suspected-pathological patterns at controlled depth, so the measurement is attributable to a specific shape rather than the library as a whole. Compare against the hcomp-en-masse alternative from the hcomp speedup note.

Output: a short writeup of which patterns are linear-vs-superlinear in depth and which are not, sufficient to decide whether Yoneda strictification actually attacks the right cost. This decision gates the broader strictification experiments outlined in the 2026-05-05 meeting notes.
Background: the original slowness observation and the hcomp-based workaround. Subtask of the Logical Relations on Display milestone.

fr:title.text: What the bookkeeping is over: unsolved metas, not an elaborated term

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: What the bookkeeping is over: unsolved metas, not an elaborated term

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Removing --allow-unsolved-metas from Real04 fails with [UnsolvedConstraints]. Same for RealFlat04. So with --lossy-unification on, Agda doesn't actually finish elaborating the proof. The body persisted to the interface is a single reference to an unsolved meta (unsolvedmeta.N) parameterised by the module's level args. The "elaborated term" I attributed the cost to in earlier drafts of this tree doesn't exist.

What does exist in the meta-store: 384 unsolved metas for Real04, 174 for RealFlat04, 73 for Real00. Each unsolved meta carries a type, a context (telescope of variables in scope), and entries on Agda's constraint list. With lossy on, Agda gives up on the trickier ones rather than recursing forever, and they remain in the store. The 11.5s of bookkeeping is over those 384 meta entries, each of which has a SETᴰ.Hom[_][_,_]-flavoured type that mentions g*Xᴰ = isFibrationSETᴰ._*_ g Xᴰ, the cartesian-product-fibration combinator, LRⱽObᴰ→LRⱽ, etc.
Direct AST measurements on the postulated-type fixtures (which DO fully elaborate, no unsolved metas) — by reflection in Bench/ReindFillerChains/SizeReflect.agda:
fr:mainmatter.html:pre: GOAL ELABORATED AST NODES AGDA WALL TIME Implicit01 55 0.87s Implicit04 688 0.90s Implicit16 8,350 0.86s Implicit32 31,334 0.87s Wrapped01 688 0.97s Wrapped04 1,507 0.98s
fr:mainmatter.html:p: Two things stand out. First, on postulated types, term size grows quadratically with chain depth — 31k nodes at depth 32. Second, none of that matters for time: those cases all check in under 1s, dominated by interface-deserialization. So size alone is not the cost driver.

The cost driver is the meta store, not the elaborated term. Each Implicit/Wrapped AST node is R.def (quote postulate) — trivial for downstream passes to look up, highlight, serialize, and the postulated fixtures fully elaborate so no metas are left behind. In the real SETᴰ setting, the analogous pieces reference deep qualified names inside the displayed-presheaf infrastructure, the unifier under lossy gives up rather than recursing, and 384 entries remain in the meta store. The cost decomposes as
fr:mainmatter.html:pre: cost ≈ (meta count) × (per-meta type complexity) × (unifier work per call)
fr:mainmatter.html:p: where the "unifier work per call" factor is what --lossy-unification bounds at typing time, and the bookkeeping passes (InverseNameLookup, Highlighting, Serialization, Miscellaneous) walk the remaining (\text {meta count}) \times (\text {per-meta type complexity}) entries post-typing. Each lever attacks a different factor and they compose multiplicatively — see the annotation experiment below for the quantitative split.

The plateau on depth (Real04=13.0s, Real16=13.4s, Real32=14.1s, Real64=14.8s — ~30ms per junction past 4) is consistent: each extra junction adds one meta with similar type complexity, so the per-junction cost is small relative to the fixed cost of the wrapping itself.

fr:title.text: Why displayed presheaves are catastrophically worse

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Why displayed presheaves are catastrophically worse

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The same wrapping pattern, applied to displayed presheaves, has each junction's Hom-type be a NatTrans (component functions + naturality). Per-meta type complexity is multiplicatively bigger. Bookkeeping cost is (\text {meta count}) \times (\text {per-meta type complexity}), so the displayed-presheaf case scales worse along the type-complexity axis even at the same chain depth.

The comment in Sets/Properties.agda hypothesised that the slowness comes from "the unification of the implicit arguments to each of these reind fillers… we may mitigate the slowness here by removing nested reindexings." Sharper picture now:

html:ul.html:li: Right that unification is implicated and type-driven. 213s without --lossy-unification on the depth-4 chain; postulated-type fixtures (Wrapped, Implicit, Explicit) cannot reproduce the slowness even at depth 32 (31,334 AST nodes), so the cost is in unifying real SETᴰ.Hom[_][_,_] types, not in the chain shape itself.

Right that filling implicits helps — but the path argument, not the type implicits. Filling {a, b, p} on every reind-filler⁻ (the Explicit fixture) doesn't move the postulated case, which was already fast. But replacing the e : a ≡ b path argument with refl on the real chain gives a 2× speedup (13.13s → 6.20s on the bench, 14.83s → 6.75s in the actual library) by short-circuiting the unifier search at each reind-filler⁻ call.

Wrong about "nested reindexings" being the lever. Cutting nesting depth only saves ~30ms per junction past depth 4 — Real04≈Real16 ≈Real64 under lossy. The proof shape's chain length is not what's expensive.

The dominant residual cost is bookkeeping over the meta store. With lossy on, typing is 1.3 percent of the total; the remaining 11.5s is post-typing work over 384 unsolved metas, set by (\text {meta count}) \times (\text {per-meta type complexity}). Lossy and explicit-refl attack the typing factor; strictification is what attacks per-meta type complexity (and shrinks the bookkeeping bill proportionally).

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Yoneda strictification is still the right fix, with a sharper reason than the original comment suggested. The win is not "the unifier sees fewer reduction obligations". The win is "each unsolved meta in the store has a smaller, simpler type", because the strictified fiber types substituted into each junction are smaller. The downstream bookkeeping passes (scope lookup, highlighting, interface build) walk those meta types and shrink proportionally.

Concrete prediction: strictification should drop Real04 from ~13s back toward Real00's ~3.4s import baseline, mostly by collapsing the Miscellaneous + InverseNameLookup + Highlighting + Serialization buckets, not the Typing bucket (which is already small under lossy).

It will not eliminate the import cost (Real00 is 3.4s with the current import graph, almost entirely in deserialization) — that's a separate concern about the size of the displayed-presheaf infrastructure being pulled in.

It does not obviate --lossy-unification: removing lossy turns the depth-4 case into 213s. The three levers attack different factors of (meta count) × (per-meta type complexity) × (unifier work per call) and are independent:

html:ul.html:li: --lossy-unification bounds unifier work per call (16×).
_ → refl annotation further cuts unifier work per call on top of lossy (2× more).
Strictification shrinks per-meta type complexity, which feeds through to both the typing cost and the post-typing bookkeeping.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: All three should be applied together. Strictification is the most invasive but addresses the largest single multiplier and the only one that touches the bookkeeping bill.

The intervention is specific to wrapped reindexing chains.

html:ul.html:li: Lossy attacks per-meta type complexity. It bounds how much work the unifier does normalizing the huge SETᴰ.Hom[_][_,_] types attached to each meta.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Meta count is essentially unchanged (384 → 389, basically noise). The user's hypothesis that "filling earlier metas resolves later ones" is not what's happening — invisible metas like _b_237, _a_276, _bᴰ.fst_358 survive both runs. fr:mainmatter.html:pre: cost ≈ (meta count) × (per-meta type complexity) × (unifier work per call) ↑ ↑ ↑ (mostly fixed (lossy attacks (annotation attacks by proof shape) this; strictifi- this) cation also)
fr:mainmatter.html:p: Practical take: in real Properties.agda code, the easy mechanical intervention reind-filler⁻ _ → reind-filler⁻ refl (where applicable) should give about a 2× speedup. It does not obviate --lossy-unification or strictification — those still own the bigger factors.

This explains the user's prior empirical observation: running C-u C-u C-c C-s (Solve constraints at strongest normalization) on ? holes returns refl-shaped solutions that, when written back into the source, give exactly this 2× speedup. The investigation here just quantifies what that interactive workflow was achieving.

Caveat: writing refl only works because, in this specific proof shape, every e : a ≡ b arising from reind-filler⁻ reduces under the rectifyOut/congᴰ wrapping to a path of compositions that collapses to refl once the implicit fiber types are pinned. In a more general chain you might need a non-trivial composite — but in that case C-u C-u C-c C-s still gives the right thing.

Decision implication: strictification + lossy + explicit refl are the three independent levers. Strictification is the most invasive but addresses the largest factor (per-meta type complexity, multiplicatively shrinks meta sizes); the _→refl cleanup is a cheap mechanical 2× before doing any structural work.

html:ul.html:li: The depth 3→4 step (Real03 = 4.07s, Real04 = 12.97s) is now understood as "first successful elaboration", not a lossy threshold. Real01–Real03 fail fast with a type-mismatch error because the chain is too short for endpoints to unify. Depth 4 is the minimum chain length that elaborates at all, at which point the post-typing bookkeeping fires. Worth confirming by a typecheck-only benchmark that disables Highlighting and Serialization, if Agda exposes the knobs.

Does the refl-annotation lever transfer to the UniversalQuantifierⱽ proof shape? ExponentialsⱽSETᴰueⱽ benefits 2× because its rectifyOut/congᴰ-wrapped chain reduces to refl once implicits are pinned. When someone is already inside that file, attempting the construction is the cheapest way to find out.

The qualitative claim ("typing under lossy is a small slice, meta-store bookkeeping dominates") holds either way.

fr:title.text: State and Attempt Löb Induction for ▷

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: State and Attempt Löb Induction for ▷

fr:mainmatter.html:p: State and attempt the Löb induction principle lob : (▷ A ⊢ A) → (⊤ ⊢ A) for the candidate ▷ of sss-00B9. This is the test of the whole approach: if Löb holds, the modality is genuinely "later"; if it fails, examine why before fixing the definition.

Sketch to follow. From ▷ A ⊢ A and next (sss-00BD) build \rhd A \vdash \rhd A as a \sqrt [w]{}-coalgebra in each component; uniqueness on each component forces the global fixed point, and the limit of "the unique fixed point" is the unique fixed point of the limit.

Compare against sss-00A8. The character-by- character flavour of the proof matches the well-founded-on-string-length recursion already used to build the Brzozowski parser. If the proof goes through, check whether it reuses that recursion verbatim — that would be evidence Löb here is the same principle, repackaged as a type former.

html:ul.html:li: The "uniqueness on each component" step might require a global productivity assumption that doesn't follow from ▷ A ⊢ A alone.
The empty-string boundary may sneak back in via the limit, even though we excluded it from the indexing.
Composing two limits (the indexed product and the recursive fixed point) may need a Fubini-style commutation that is genuinely nontrivial.

Define and verify next : A ⊢ ▷ A for the candidate ▷ of sss-00B9.

Verification check. fr:title.text: Resolution: next is structure, not a theorem

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Resolution: next is structure, not a theorem

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The diagram chase does not go through for arbitrary grammars — the verification check anticipated above fails. next is not derivable from the indexed-product definition of ▷ alone; it requires extra structure on A.

Max's framing. Presheaves on (\texttt {String}, \text {suffix-order}) are precisely \Box -coalgebras over families. The map next : A ⊢ ▷ A is the coalgebra structure, not a global term. So instead of postulating it (or holding it open as a hole), package it as a record:
fr:mainmatter.html:pre: record IsCoalgebra (A : Grammar ℓA) : Type ℓA where field next : A ⊢ ▷ A
fr:mainmatter.html:p: The canonical example is ⊤-IsCoalgebra: ⊤ is suffix-closed because any suffix of a ⊤-parse is a ⊤-parse. This lives in Grammar/Later/Coalgebra.agda on the guarded branch of gsa-brzozowski.

html:ul.html:li: Grammar/Later/Base.agda now compiles without --allow-unsolved-metas — the held-open next hole is gone.
Löb (sss-00BE) goes through unchanged: the obstruction to next does not block Löb, because Löb is proven directly by well-founded recursion on string length and never invokes a global next.

This is the same shape of design discovery as Cass's recursive-coalgebra framework: well-foundedness + recursion lives on coalgebra structures, not on bare grammars. The connection is made explicit in the recursive-coalgebra synthesis — next is the coalgebra structure that feeds a c2a-morphism.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Agentic programming on multiple feature branches is most natural with one git worktree per branch plus direnv for an automatic Nix dev shell per directory. But each .direnv becomes a GC root that pins its full flake-input closure, and these accumulate — the April 2026 cleanup found 157 direnv-originated GC roots across 11 project dirs in ~, most of them stale.

Shared flake-inputs cache at a stable path so multiple worktrees of the same repo reuse one closure instead of pinning N copies.

direnv allow gating: only allow direnv in active worktrees; require explicit re-allow when returning to a dormant one.

fr:title.text: forester-apple-sync blocks the Emacs daemon event loop

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: forester-apple-sync blocks the Emacs daemon event loop

fr:mainmatter.html:p: sync.sh invokes forester-apple-sync via emacsclient --eval '(forester-apple-sync)'. Because emacsclient --eval runs the function synchronously in the Emacs daemon's event loop, and forester-apple-sync makes one blocking osascript call per TODO, the entire Emacs process is unresponsive for the full duration of the sync (up to several seconds). The sync fires every 30 minutes via launchd, so this happens silently in the background and is easy to miss until it coincides with active editing.

There is no reason the daemon needs to be involved here at all — sync.sh already has a emacs --batch fallback path for when the daemon is unavailable. The batch path should be preferred for non-interactive bulk work, not just used as a fallback.

html:ul.html:li: Prefer batch over daemon for sync. Invert the sync.sh logic: always use emacs --batch -l ~/ocaml-forester/forester-org.el --eval '(forester-apple-sync)' for the launchd-triggered sync. The daemon path (emacsclient) can remain for manual SPC r s invocations where interactive feedback is wanted.

Run async inside the daemon. If the daemon path is kept, wrap the bulk sync body in make-process or async-start so osascript calls do not block the event loop. This is more complex but also fixes the SPC r s interactive path.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: See Automate Apple Reminders and Calendar sync for Forester TODOs for the broader sync architecture.

Server configuration lives in ~/nix-config/hosts/macproseph/. The sync pipeline is documented in Forest Sync and Capture Architecture; the capture server's kick_sync flow (which chains forest-pull.service → forest-build.service) is described in Forest capture server.
Possible causes to investigate:

html:ul.html:li: forest-build.service not triggering after a pull-only sync (i.e. when macproseph pulls from origin but no capture happened, so kick_sync never fires)
forester build running before the pull completes, so new trees aren't on disk yet when the build reads inputs
Caddy serving stale output from a previous build — check whether caddy is configured with file_server pointing at the live output/ directory or a cached copy
Datalog query cache inside forester not invalidated across builds (less likely; forester rebuilds from scratch)
The systemd timer for forest-pull.service not actually firing — verify with systemctl status forest-pull.timer and journalctl -u forest-pull.service

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Debugging checklist:

html:ul.html:li: SSH into macproseph; confirm new tree files are present under /home/steven/forest/trees/

fr:title.text: Claude skills for iterative Agda development

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Claude skills for iterative Agda development

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Design and ship one or more Claude Code skills that help an agent draft Agda code iteratively, using the Agda typechecker as the primary oracle instead of reading through the codebase until the context window is exhausted. Any pre-existing Agda skill is unused and should be treated as deprecated — replace rather than extend it.
Core iteration loop. The skill should enforce a hole-at-a-time workflow:

html:ul.html:li: Query the types and contexts of all open holes in the target file up front, so the agent has a work plan before editing.

For each hole, make one modular change, then typecheck. Do not advance to the next hole until the current edit typechecks cleanly and no unsolved metas (yellow) remain — yellow is failure, not success.
When stuck, prefer re-introducing {! !} over committing a guess. Let the compiler narrow the goal.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Runtime is a signal, not just a cost. Every typecheck and every agda --interaction command runs under a wall-clock budget:

html:ul.html:li: Hard cap around 20s per check or interaction — if Agda hasn't responded, treat the attempt as failed and abandon that route. Do not wait longer hoping it resolves.

Anything over ~5s is a warning sign for the vast majority of goals. Slow elaboration usually means the agent is fighting the typechecker: wrong lemma driving divergent unification, universe mismatch blowing up constraints, over-concrete instantiation, or reduction that should have been abstract / opaque. Treat the slowness as evidence the approach is wrong, not as something to wait out.

Prune aggressively on slow feedback. When a candidate term makes the typechecker crawl, back it out and try a structurally different approach (different lemma, different case-split order, more holes) rather than tweaking details of the slow term.
Some files legitimately take longer (large HITs, heavy transports). Allow a per-project override, but default to the tight budget.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Use the compiler as an oracle, not the codebase. Wrap agda --interaction (or --interaction-json) in a bash script so the agent can issue Cmd_goal_type_context_infer, Cmd_refine_or_intro, Cmd_make_case, Cmd_auto_maybe_all, and Cmd_compute programmatically. These narrowing tactics produce correct-by-construction skeletons and are far higher density than reading source.
Context-management rules (the failure mode to prevent: agent reads through stdlib / cubical until the window fills, compacts, then repeats without writing code):

html:ul.html:li: Prefer grep over Read for lemma discovery. Type signatures are one-liners; whole-file reads are almost never necessary.

Delegate library search to a subagent with a tight prompt ("find functions in Cubical.Foundations.* whose return type matches isEquiv _") so exploration fills the subagent's context, not the main one.
Exhaust the typechecker first. Before reading any file, the agent must have run goal/context inspection, auto, refine, and case-split on the current hole.
Budget exploration explicitly: at most N files read before the next compile attempt. When the budget is hit, write something so the typechecker's error narrows the search further.
Scratch-file discovered lemmas (Module.foo : T → U) so post-compaction the agent doesn't re-discover the same results.
Fail loudly. After K consecutive edits without a green typecheck, surface the blockage to the user rather than spiraling.
Single monolithic skill vs. several small ones (e.g. agda-fill-hole, agda-search-lemma, agda-check)?
Does the skill need project-aware setup (locate .agda-lib / Cubical / agda-stdlib roots) or can it assume the user's environment is already configured?
How should the skill handle Agsy timeouts and partial results from auto?
Cubical vs. vanilla Agda — same skill, or separate flavors for --cubical pragmas and HITs?

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Next steps. Prototype the bash wrapper around agda --interaction-json, sketch the skill's SKILL.md frontmatter and trigger conditions, then dogfood on an open hole in Cubical.Categories.Double.Instances.Displayed or similar WIP Agda work.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The first bulk push from forester-apple-sync crashed on this very tree. The cause: forester-org--parse-meta is a regex that scans the entire file rather than only the frontmatter. The body originally contained an example showing how the apple-id meta is written, embedded in a ... block. The parser treated that example as a real frontmatter declaration, extracted its placeholder value as the apple-id, and fed it to AppleScript, which failed with Invalid index (-1719). The literal example is omitted from this tree on purpose to avoid re-triggering the bug.

Workaround applied. The prose on line 23 was rewritten to describe the meta entry by name rather than embedding the literal markup. This is a hack — any future tree that documents this meta key by writing the literal markup would re-trigger the bug.
